#3124. BellRing (BRBR) Q4 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Management pivots fiscal 2027 toward cost cuts as price hikes test volume.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 18, 2026 at 3:55PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

BellRing (BRBR +24.07%) reported fourth-quarter results that exceeded revenue expectations while management initiated a comprehensive strategic review and withdrew previous long-term financial targets. Management indicated that fiscal 2027 will serve as a transitional year focused on structural cost reductions and operational efficiency rather than aggressive top-line expansion. The company is implementing a strategic supply chain optimization program to offset significant commodity inflation and restore gross margins. Despite near-term volume pressure from pricing actions, management is prioritizing distribution expansion into the convenience and grocery channels to diversify beyond its core club and mass retail footprint.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for standing by. Welcome to the BellRing Brands Fourth Quarter Fiscal Year 2026 Earnings Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I would like now to turn the conference over to Jennifer Meyer, Investor Relations for BellRing Brands. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Meyer: Good morning, and thank you for joining us today for BellRing Brands Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2026 Earnings Call. With me today are Mike Axelrod, our President and CEO; and Paul Rode, our CFO. Mike and Paul will begin with prepared remarks, and afterwards, we'll have a brief question-and-answer session. The press release and supplemental slide presentation that support these remarks are posted on our website in both the Investor Relations and the SEC filings sections of bellring.com. In addition, the release and slides are available on the SEC's website.

Before we continue, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties that should be carefully considered by investors as actual results could differ materially from these statements. These forward-looking statements are current as of the date of this call, and management undertakes no obligation to update these statements. As a reminder, this call is being recorded, and an audio replay will be available on our website. And finally, this call will discuss certain non-GAAP measures. For a reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to the nearest GAAP measure, see our press release issued this morning and posted on our website.

With that, I will turn the call over to Mike.

Michael Axelrod: Thank you, Jennifer, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining our fourth quarter earnings call. Let me begin with a brief recap of the fourth quarter before sharing my initial assessment and priorities for the business. Fourth quarter net sales growth of 7% exceeded our expectations with both Premier Protein and Dymatize contributing to the upside. Premier shake dollar consumption grew 9% with low teens volume growth, while continuing to add households. This growth exceeded our expectations, driven by stronger-than-planned volumes in the important back-to-school selling period. Promotional discounts levels were in line with our plans. While the category promotional environment remained elevated, intensity moderated somewhat in Q4 relative to Q2.

Adjusted EBITDA was $66 million, within our guidance range and included additional inventory-related charges from our year-end inventory review. Underlying profitability was modestly better than expected, but remains well below the levels we believe the business can achieve. Before discussing our plans for 2027, I'd like to share 2 important conclusions from my first 100 days. First, BellRing has an exceptional foundation, strong brands, attractive category dynamics, loyal consumers and meaningful scale. Second, we have opportunities to translate those advantages into stronger competitive performance and profitability. We need to become more agile, more cost competitive and more disciplined in how we invest and execute. Those changes are already underway.

I'll start with the strengths that give me confidence in our long-term potential before turning to where I believe we need to raise the bar. We operate in a healthy category supported by attractive consumer health and wellness trends. The RTD shake category grew 11% in fiscal 2026, supported by double-digit volume growth and continues to stand out as one of the few food and beverage categories delivering meaningful volume growth. We expect the category to deliver high single-digit dollar growth in 2027 with considerable long-term growth opportunity as household penetration remains below that of mature CPG categories. Within this attractive category, Premier Protein has established a leading position and strong consumer foundation.

At approximately 23% and growing, the brand leads the category in household penetration. This demonstrates meaningful consumer awareness and adoption while leaving room to reach new households and support future growth. Importantly, Premier's taste ratings are among the best in the category, and it maintains the highest repeat purchase rate in RTDs. These are compelling indicators of the strength of our consumer proposition and the loyalty we've built. As a category leader, we play an essential role in helping our retail and supply partners capitalize on category growth, creating a strong foundation for collaboration and shared success. Premier has established a powerful presence across channels, including the category's largest and fastest growing.

We hold leading positions in club and mass, the 2 largest channels by volume as well as the #1 position on the leading e-commerce platform, a key driver of category growth. Our scale extends to our supply chain where we are one of the category's largest purchasers of protein ingredients and co-manufacturing capacity, which gives us strategic relevance and opportunity to work closely with our partners to drive efficiencies. While these strengths reinforce my confidence in our long-term potential, I see clear areas of opportunity. We have talented people and strong brands, but our capabilities and ways of working have not always kept pace with the growth and complexity of the business. I've identified 3 clear opportunities to improve performance.

First, strengthen our commercial execution through better consumer insights, more effective marketing and innovation and deeper partnerships with our retailer partners; second, leverage our scale to structurally improve our cost position; and third, increase the speed, agility and accountability with which we operate. Improved insights and analytic capabilities will help us develop more targeted, impactful product innovation that drives household penetration and purchase frequency and improves returns on promotional and marketing spending. Equally important is elevating business planning with our retail partners to unlock opportunities and drive share growth. Beyond strengthening our commercial capabilities, we must fully capture our scale and category leadership advantage in our cost structure.

We are advancing a strategic supply chain optimization program targeting at least $100 million in gross savings over the next 3 years. These opportunities span manufacturing, procurement, packaging and logistics. We expect to begin realizing benefits in fiscal 2027 with savings building over time. These structural improvements will provide greater flexibility to reinvest in our brands, offset inflation and strengthen profitability. And finally, we must establish clear ownership to enable faster decision-making while better leveraging our existing tools and systems and making targeted investments where needed. As part of this effort, we will be enhancing integrated business planning and financial visibility to enable stronger execution and more consistent performance.

We are taking action now to capitalize on these opportunities while advancing a broader strategic review to shape the next phase of our long-term growth. This review is focused on strengthening our competitive position, improving profitability and establishing a more sustainable growth model. As part of this process, we believe it's appropriate to withdraw our previous long-term algorithm issued last November. We intend to share our refreshed strategy and updated long-term financial outlook with our second quarter earnings call in May 2027. We recognize the importance of a clear long-term target for investors and look forward to sharing the results of our work. Turning to 2027.

We expect 2027 to be a year of foundational progress as we build operational capabilities and deliver margin expansion while absorbing modest near-term top line pressure. The fiscal 2027 outlook should not be viewed as indicative of our long-term financial potential of our business. We expect Premier RTD consumption to grow in mid-single digits, below expected category growth and are focused on narrowing that gap through execution. We expect BellRing sales -- BellRing net sales of up 1% to down 3% with Premier Shake sales trailing consumption growth. This reflects 2 dynamics: a moderation in distribution growth this year as we lap outsized prior year comparisons and modest retailer inventory adjustments associated with our pricing actions.

We view these factors as largely 2027 transitional impacts. Our focus is on improving velocities across existing distribution, expanding in underpenetrated channels and delivering innovation that drives incremental consumption and sustainable growth. Our sales guidance reflects a prudent approach that includes a range of outcomes for several key variables. We expect price increase related elasticity impacts greater than one, continued competitive pressure in the club channel and benefits from innovation. As a result of our Q1 price increase, promotional planning with certain FDM retail partners remains ongoing. We expect to secure merchandising opportunities as plans are finalized and have incorporated a range of outcomes into our guidance.

We expect to make progress on adjusted EBITDA in 2027 with benefits of pricing, cost-saving initiatives and lapping 2026 inventory items somewhat offset by continued commodity and freight inflation. Overall, while we expect our low double-digit price increases on shakes to create some near-term headwinds, we believe it is necessary to restore profitability in light of significant inflationary pressures across key commodities. To deliver our financial plan, we're focused on 4 operating priorities in 2027. One, reducing the cost of our core shakes; two, strengthening market share through improved club performance and targeted distribution expansion; three, increasing our effectiveness of our marketing and innovation investments; and four, building the operational capabilities and accountability needed to execute consistently.

With respect to our first priority, our historical focus was to ensure we had sufficient supply to support rapid growth in demand against the backdrop of tight industry capacity. With industry capacity constraints easing, we are now implementing structural cost reductions and expect to deliver approximately $25 million of our 3-year cost savings program in 2027. These savings will be driven by optimizing our co-manufacturing network, improving procurement economics and reducing distribution and packaging costs. Second, we intend to improve our share trends over time by regaining momentum in our core channels, while continuing to expand distribution and improving our promotional effectiveness.

Club remains a critical channel for Premier in the category, and we recognize that sustaining leadership requires continuous innovation and strong customer partnerships. As a result of our improved joint business planning, we expect to recover a previously lost everyday assortment item late in the first quarter. Additionally, we are pleased with how our innovation tests in club performed this year and are planning for additional test opportunities in fiscal '27 grounded in the needs of club members. This month, we began shipping Premier Ultimate 42-gram shakes for a regional club test. Alongside our efforts to strengthen performance in our largest channel, we remain focused on expanding distribution across other channels.

In 2027, we expect to grow Premier distribution through meaningful gains in grocery, where our portfolio continues to be undershelved relative to its potential as well as entering DSD. We are executing a regional expansion strategy in DSD in parallel with ongoing efforts to secure a national partnership. Our regional strategy is a disciplined targeted strategy for both core 30-gram and Ultimate Protein shakes. We have secured contracts with over 25 distributors reaching 10 states and are in active discussions with several distributors to further expand our coverage in 2027. We are also pleased to announce that we have secured distribution with several national C-store retail chains and have activation and marketing plans to ensure strong velocities in this channel.

Volume is shipping this quarter with consumption following in Q2, and we expect DSD to contribute approximately 1 point to BellRing revenue in 2027. Across channels, we are undertaking a broader assessment of our promotional strategy to ensure our trade investments are delivering the greatest impact. We've identified targeted opportunities to enhance return on investment in 2027 and apply these learnings to our programs for this year. Overall, our focus is on strengthening our competitive position across channels while laying the foundation for a return to growth in club over time. Third, we are taking a more focused and disciplined approach to marketing and innovation to maximize the impact and returns of our investments.

We are increasing advertising support while refining our marketing strategy to strengthen consumer engagement and maximize the effectiveness of our spending. Our 2026 campaign delivered lifts in awareness, purchase intent and brand favorability, but did not achieve our return-on-investment goals. The 2027 marketing plan is designed to engage consumers across the full path to purchase with refreshed creative, more precise audience targeting and a greater emphasis on driving conversion. Our objective is to recruit new households, increase purchase frequency among existing consumers and improve the return on our marketing investment.

We are launching our New Year, New You campaign earlier this -- earlier with refreshed Go Get 'Em creative beginning in December to build awareness and purchase intent ahead of January. Looking ahead, we plan to introduce a new brand campaign grounded in rigorous testing for the fourth quarter back-to-school promotion season with stronger differentiation and a focus on consumer acquisition and loyalty. We also have new partnerships with leading media and shopper agencies. These partners will help us improve audience targeting, optimize our media, strengthen demand generation and engage consumers closer to the point of purchase, including through retail media. We will measure success by strong conversion and improved returns, not spending alone.

Our 2027 agenda is focused on discipline, prioritizing opportunities that begin to address differentiation on our core 30-gram shakes and new products that create incremental category growth and expand occasions. We intend to evaluate innovation against clear consumer and financial milestones. For our core portfolio, we are advancing cleaner formulations, differentiated packaging and consumer communications and continuing our successful LTO strategy. On formulation, this summer, we launched the carrageenan-free formula at a key retailer -- club retailer and broader formulation work is ongoing. We will share more later this part as we -- as part of our strategic review.

Our limited time offerings continue to perform well with Pumpkin Spice in the top tertile, and we will build on that momentum with a unique new seasonal shake flavor launching in our second quarter. Last, as part of our core portfolio work, we are also making targeted investments to update Dymatize's positioning. We will focus on packaging and messaging improvements to more clearly communicate the consumer benefits of Dymatize's best-in-class formula and high-quality ingredients. This year, our new product efforts are focused on fewer opportunities with the potential to expand occasions and deliver meaningful incremental growth.

Our priorities include building momentum behind the Premier Ultimate 42-gram and increasing consumer awareness, trial and repeat purchase for Sparkling Soda, both of which were launched in late fiscal 2026. We're also expanding our successful Coffee House line. In closing, BellRing has strong brands, a leading market position and significant opportunities ahead. Our responsibility now is to translate those advantages into stronger and more consistent performance. Fiscal 2027 is a year of action. I am confident in the opportunities ahead, but equally clear that success requires urgency, focus and accountability. We have the team, brands and scale to compete more effectively, and we are committed to delivering the results that our shareholders expect.

I look forward to updating you on our progress and sharing our long-term strategy later this year. Finally, I want to thank our team for their hard work, dedication and commitment to our business. We have important work ahead of us, and I appreciate the energy and focus our people are bringing to building a stronger company. Before turning the call to Paul, I want to briefly address the CFO transition that we announced today. First, I want to thank Paul for his leadership and contributions over the past decade. He played an instrumental role in BellRing's IPO and subsequent growth and has been a valued partner to me during my first few months as CEO.

I appreciate his continued support through this transition. I'm also excited to welcome Travis Leonard as our new CFO effective December 1. Travis brings extensive financial leadership experience, including serving as CFO of Hostess Brands and Lockton. His experience driving profitable growth, operational discipline and capital allocation will be valuable as we execute our strategy. With that, I'll turn the call over to Paul.

Paul Rode: Thank you, Mike, for the kind words, and good morning, everyone. It has been an honor to serve as BellRing's CFO since our IPO, and I am proud of what we've built together. I've been fortunate to work with an amazing team at BellRing and at our former parent company, Post Holdings. I'm grateful to my colleagues for their partnership and support along the way. I feel great about the opportunity ahead for BellRing, and I'll be working closely with Mike and Travis to make this transition as smooth as possible. Turning to our results and outlook.

Category fundamentals remained healthy in the fourth quarter with total wellness dollar sales up 8% and RTD shake dollar sales up 12%, driven by strong volume growth. Promotional intensity remained elevated year-over-year. However, the percentage of sales sold on promotion moderated somewhat in Q4 relative to Q2. Premier RTD consumption growth of 9% was ahead of our expectation of mid-single digits. We were encouraged by improving trends in this club channel with consumption turning slightly positive. Consumption, excluding club, remained strong, up 17% in the quarter, with each of the mass, food and e-commerce channels delivering double-digit growth. Net sales exceeded our expectations, up 7% year-over-year. Premier Protein brand sales grew 7% with RTD net sales up 8%.

RTD volume grew 17%, partially offset by a 9% decline in price/mix. The RTD outperformance versus our guidance was primarily driven by volume. As contemplated in our guidance, total BellRing net sales growth included a 2-point benefit from the Ultimate and Sparkling innovation launches. Dymatize sales were up 4% with strong price/mix of 18% and a 14% volume decline. International sales were strong, while domestic volume declines were driven by elasticities related to inflation-driven price increases taken earlier this year. Compared to our expectations, Dymatize outperformed in e-commerce and mass. Adjusted gross profit was $139 million with adjusted gross margin of 20.1% compared to 29.7% a year ago.

The year-over-year decline was driven by significant protein and freight cost inflation, including tariffs and incremental trade investment. Additionally, we recorded $16 million in inventory-related headwinds, which had an unfavorable 230 basis point impact on gross margin. SG&A expenses were $80 million or 11.6% of net sales, including a $3 million advertising increase. The quarter also benefited from lower incentive compensation and modest savings from our organizational realignment earlier this year. Adjusted EBITDA was $66 million at a margin of 9.6%. This included the $16 million of inventory actions that I discussed earlier, which had an unfavorable impact of 230 basis points. Turning to our fiscal 2027 outlook.

We expect BellRing net sales of $2.32 billion to $2.42 billion, representing a range of 1% growth to down 3% versus prior year. This is inclusive of an approximately 100 basis point headwind from powders and Dymatize, with Premier Shakes expected to be up 2% to down 2%. As a result of the trade inventory dynamics that Mike discussed, we expect shipment growth to trail consumption growth, creating a mid-single-digit headwind to net sales growth. Our outlook incorporates a price increase of low double digits on shakes, along with additional price increases on powders, both effective at the beginning of fiscal 2027. From a brand perspective, we expect mid-single-digit Premier shake consumption growth.

Premier net sales are expected to decline 1% at the midpoint, in line with the overall company, inclusive of an approximate 100 basis point headwind from powders. Meaningful price growth should be offset by volume declines from consumer elasticities and trade inventory headwinds. In addition, we expect volume headwinds as we lap a year of strong distribution gains and retailers modestly adjust their inventory as a result of our price increase. We expect Dymatize and all other to decline low single digits at the midpoint, driven by consumer elasticities. Moving to fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA. We expect adjusted EBITDA of $310 million to $350 million or approximately a 14% margin at the midpoint versus a 12% margin in 2026.

The approximate 200 basis points of margin improvement will be driven by meaningful gross margin expansion of nearly 400 points. This improvement will be partially offset by 100 basis points of incremental A&P investment and higher SG&A resulting from a return to normalized incentive compensation levels and capability investments. Adjusted gross margin expansion largely reflects the benefits of low double-digit pricing, cost savings of approximately $25 million and favorable comparisons to 2026 inventory-related items. This is partially offset by high single-digit commodity inflation inclusive of tariffs. As Mike discussed, our full year sales guidance range reflects several meaningful variables, and these will primarily play out after the first quarter.

I'll now walk through those factors and how they influence our first quarter versus balance of year outlook. Our price increase was actioned at the beginning of our fiscal year with retailer implementation on shelf continuing to phase in. As a result, retailer inventory adjustments are beginning to impact the first quarter while more meaningful consumer elasticity impacts remain ahead of us. The New Year, New You and back-to-school seasons, which are typically more competitive and promotional, are still ahead of us in our second and fourth quarters. Ongoing FDM promotional discussions that primarily impact consumption in Q2 have an unfavorable year-over-year impact on shipments in the first quarter.

And last, distribution and innovation comparisons are tougher as we move through the year. With that context, we anticipate Premier RTD consumption growth to be low to mid-teens in the first quarter and BellRing net sales growth to be up low single digits. Premier is expected to be in line with the overall company, inclusive of an approximate 100 basis point headwind from powders. Price/mix is expected to increase double digits, reflecting our price increase, which will be mostly offset by volume declines. Dymatize and all other sales are expected to be relatively in line with the overall company. The meaningful gap between consumption and shipments for Premier Protein RTDs in the first quarter is driven by several factors.

These include lapping prior year shipment builds associated with a mass promotion and new products. The timing lag between our price increase and shelf changes is favorable to consumer consumption, while we expect some headwinds to shipments from retailer inventory adjustments. We expect Q1 adjusted EBITDA margin to be just under 17% at the midpoint with gross margin expansion offset -- largely offset by the timing of incremental advertising spend. Note that the timing shift in our new year programming will put some advertising spend forward into the quarter. Additionally, we are lapping our lowest quarterly advertising spend quarter from the prior year.

We expect gross margin expansion in each quarter of the year, although the cadence of year-over-year improvement will be influenced by the comparison against inventory-related charges in the second, third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2026. Our cost savings outlook is evenly phased across the year. At current prices, year-over-year freight inflation is expected to be highest in the first quarter and moderating throughout the year, while protein inflation compared to prior year is expected to remain relatively consistent through the year. With respect to SG&A, incremental advertising investments are expected to be more heavily weighted to the first and fourth quarters while incentive compensation headwinds are more meaningful post the first quarter.

As a result of all of these factors, we expect higher year-over-year adjusted EBITDA margin expansion in the second half versus the first half. Absent the fiscal '26 inventory-related comparisons, adjusted EBITDA margin expansion is relatively even between the first and second halves of fiscal '27. Turning to our balance sheet and capital allocation priorities. Our business generated strong cash flow in 2026 with operating cash flow of $126 million, inclusive of the $90 million litigation settlement payment this year. Fourth quarter cash flow was stronger than expected, resulting in a year-end net leverage ratio of 3.6x, lower than anticipated.

Looking ahead, we expect strong cash conversion in fiscal 2027, which combined with our expected adjusted EBITDA growth positions us to reduce leverage below 3x. We remain committed to a balanced capital allocation strategy that includes returning cash to shareholders and conservatively managing leverage. In summary, we remain confident in the long-term opportunity for BellRing. The steps we are taking to improve profitability, together with our strong cash flow profile, position the company well to both invest in growth opportunities and to deliver shareholder value. I will now turn it over to the operator for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] The first question will come from Andrew Lazar with Barclays.

Andrew Lazar: I guess I wanted to talk a little bit more about the promotional environment in RTDs. You mentioned that RTD volume sold on promotion in the fourth quarter was up 5 points year-over-year, but down a point versus the second quarter. I was hoping to get a better understanding of, I guess, what more specifically I meant to take away from that? Is it that promotion is up year-over-year, but you think has peaked going into '27? Or is it too early to sort of suggest that? And then what are you seeing with respect to pricing from a competitive perspective, given all the pricing you're taking? Is that fairly consistent with what you're seeing across the category?

Or is there some disparity there that we should be sort of attending to as well?

Michael Axelrod: Yes. So Andrew, so I think promotions remain an important part of our -- of competing in the category. And I don't believe the answer is just more promotions. I think the focus needs to be on the effectiveness and getting the right return from those events. We've already adjusted our '27 programs based on what we learned in 2026, and we learned a lot. We learned a lot about depth. We learned a lot about how wide, what periods of time. I think longer term, the opportunity is really to improve the ROI, continue to attract incremental households and build sustainable consumption rather than just increasing our frequency or depth.

As part of our strategy review, we're going to go a little deeper here. But I would also say we're doing a much better job in identifying and implementing quality promotion opportunities. I mean we've -- as we've expanded in FDM, we've gotten much better at learning how to -- where to place our displays, what to place in the displays, what pricing works, et cetera. And so we'll continue to expand that and continue to expand those learnings. In club, I think our plans are broadly consistent with '26. But I think as we're -- again, as we're learning, we're going to take a deeper look at frequency, timing and effectiveness as part of the review.

Paul Rode: And Andrew, I think from a category perspective, I think the call out there is just we did see a pretty intense competitive promotional activity in Q2. That moderated some in Q4. I think it's too early to tell how that plays out in fiscal '27. We've considered a number of outcomes in our guidance for that. But I think that was the call out really was just the Q4 headwind was not quite what we saw in Q2.

Andrew Lazar: And then just the competitive pricing arena as well. Have others basically been essentially keeping pace with what you're putting -- implementing in the marketplace? Or are there some disparities we should be aware of?

Paul Rode: Yes. I mean we've seen, as we called out before, I mean, some of our larger competitors took pricing earlier this year. We have seen some additional pricing actions taken in the category more recently. So again, more to come, but we have seen some pricing just with the level of inflation that's out there. I think it's logical that you'd see a lot of competitors -- it's not -- it's logical to see some of that pricing offsetting the inflation.

Operator: And our next question is going to come from Tom Palmer with JPMorgan.

Thomas Palmer: Paul, it's been great working with you over the years. I appreciate your regular availability and insights. Mike, a lot of detail in the prepared remarks. I wanted to make sure I understood messaging on this promotional activity on club and mass. There was reference to regaining in club. So should we be thinking about there were promotional events that you've been running the last couple of years, like these month-long promotions at club that will not be run that you're not sure if you're going to run? I know there was also the new promotional event last year that was added in a couple of spots.

I just -- like what promotion is still kind of to be determined versus what is secured at this point?

Paul Rode: Yes, I can start. So thank you for the kind words. So from a club perspective, we expect the promotional cadence and we expect to be similar year-over-year. So there's no significant change in the club dynamics from a promotional calendar perspective. So no change. What we were calling out in our prepared remarks is that there are still some of our merchandising and promotional programs within FDM that are still being discussed. So some of those are not fully locked in at this point. And so for guidance purposes, we've explored a range -- or we have a range of outcomes within our guidance to reflect potential outcomes there.

The other piece in your question is that within club, we called out on the last call that we expected a headwind in '27 from losing a pallet position in one of our key club customers. That now has been -- we now are regaining that. So in the prepared remarks, we talked about regaining that. So that becomes less of a headwind. There's still a little bit of a headwind in Q1 because it was off for a little bit, now it's back, but that was really to call out.

So from a club perspective, pretty similar distribution versus a year ago with some gap there in Q1 and then similar promotional dynamics from a cadence and timing perspective for club.

Operator: And our next question will come from David Palmer with Evercore.

David Palmer: Mike, a question for you on just distribution comparisons and inventory reductions that you mentioned. I know on the other hand, there's a little bit of hope out there that you'll find some distribution wins in ready-to-drink convenience channel expansion. Could you talk about that as a priority for the company? And then sort of separately, perhaps relatedly, could you talk about innovation as sort of a priority relative to past years? Could you talk about the performance of some of your recent innovation and how innovation will play into your 2027 plans?

Michael Axelrod: So first, I think in terms of the distribution TDPs, I think we continue to grow TDPs, although we're lapping a pretty significant gain in 2026. And I believe that there are meaningful opportunities ahead. I think as we scale beyond $2 billion in revenue, the impact of those distribution gains will naturally moderate. But I see meaningful opportunity here. I think grocery and convenience are particularly attractive. I think innovation and improved velocities can drive growth in more of these established channels. And so I do see continued upside there. On the innovation side, I think in terms of the solutions that we have, I think they're really promising.

I think Ultimate Sparkling and Coffee House, which we introduced this year are addressing really different consumer needs and occasions. I think Ultimate gives us an offering in the higher protein segment. And I'm pleased with the early reception by retailers and consumers. And it's going to be one of our key products that we're going to be expanding in the convenience store channel. You may have seen the announcement that we made earlier this week about a large convenience store where Ultimate is going to be a key product for us. I think Sparkling adds refreshment occasions and has the potential to be highly incremental to our product portfolio, but it's a subcategory.

It's a new category, and I think it's still in its earlier stage. I think importantly, we do need a stronger and more consistent innovation pipeline. We are evaluating our insights, our consumer insights and our innovation processes and speed to market so we can get the things -- the right things to market quicker. Innovation takes time, but we are moving with a sense of urgency to build a more impactful pipeline, including evaluation of some of our formula optimization, which I mentioned in my prepared remarks around clean label and things of that nature and really renovating the core shake as well.

Operator: And the next question is going to come from Peter Grom with UBS.

Peter Grom: Paul, thanks so much for all the help over the years as well. Mike, I wanted to get your perspective just on kind of long-term targets. And I think we can all appreciate the decision to withdraw them this morning from what was outlined a year ago. But we're still operating in a pretty volatile and uncertain environment. The category dynamics continue to evolve. So just maybe some thoughts on how you're approaching building to these targets over the next few months. What are you trying to learn? What are some of the key watch points? And then specifically, why is it important to have long-term targets at this stage?

Michael Axelrod: So I think as we're -- at this point, we're continuing to undergo our strategic review. So in terms of the longer term, I'll hold comments around what I think the long-term potential of the business is. I think '27 is a year of -- in many ways of resetting expectations. We have a tremendous amount of potential in areas that, quite frankly, are under our control.

And so I see really significant improvements around the investments we're making in promotions, again, learning and coming back with better ROI there, accelerating some of our innovation, making decisions faster and then structurally resetting our -- lowering our cost of our core shakes, which is, I think, a tremendous amount of opportunity there. So until we're through the strategy planning process here, I think the business has a tremendous potential. I just don't want to commit to anything until we've done our due diligence here.

Operator: And our next question is going to come from Alexia Howard with Bernstein.

Alexia Howard: Thank you so much to Paul, appreciate all the help. Can I ask about what price elasticity assumptions you're making as you think about the forecast, obviously, on the sales line? It obviously looks as though you've got some headwinds from distribution and other inventory adjustments. But in terms of the core consumption trends, what are you assuming?

Michael Axelrod: So we're -- thanks, Alexia. We're modeling a range of elasticities that are all greater than 1. And as our guidance would indicate, the high end of that is at the lowest elasticity, which is above 1 and the midpoint and low end would be higher. Underpinning that is we've used historical data and made additional assumptions given the magnitude of the price increase. But I'd say that's in our ranges included our best estimate in those ranges that we just communicated.

Operator: And our next question is going to come from Max Gumport with BNP.

Max Andrew Gumport: With regard to cost inflation, you gave your outlook for the year, but I was hoping you could give some color on how much of that is hedged already or covered? Just we have a sense for how much variability there still could be with regard to cost inflation this fiscal year?

Paul Rode: Sure. Yes. So we're modeling high single-digit commodity inflation in fiscal '27, which we are -- which is covered by our pricing. Most of that is at the protein cost level. So both whey powders, which is the input cost for our powder business and also milk proteins, which is the input -- primary input cost for our shake are significantly higher over the year. To your point, we do have a hedging program in place where we do have coverage, and that allows us to mitigate some of the volatility in those headwinds as we go into the year. So from a coverage perspective, our proteins are about 2/3 covered.

You may recall on freight, we had some volatility as well in '27 or '26 on freight. And so we have changed some of our strategy to some degree on the spot buy and moved some of that to contracts, which gives us kind of 3- to 6-month visibility. So we have better visibility in the first half on freight. And if you look at the rest of our basket, our input basket, we have a pretty good line of sight. So -- so our coverage is pretty solid going into the year, obviously, more covered in the first half than perhaps in the latter parts of the year. But overall, we're pretty covered.

Michael Axelrod: And just overall, we're probably covered about 70% hedged on proteins at this point.

Operator: And our next question will come from Jim Salera with Stephens.

James Salera: Paul, it's been a pleasure to work with you over the years. I appreciate all the help with the understanding the business. Mike, I wanted to go back to an earlier question about the pallet position in one of your big club customers. Can you just give us any color on what led to the initial decision to have that come out and then maybe some details on what brought it back in because that seems like a pretty quick reversal. And I'm wondering if there was a supply issue with the replacement pallet or the velocity didn't hold up.

Anything you can give us there would be helpful just to kind of understand how that might influence other retail decisions moving forward?

Michael Axelrod: Yes. I think some of it comes back to ensuring that we have -- as I've been in my first 100 days here, really looking at lots of different areas of the organization. One of them is are we organized across all of our functions to win. I think one of the areas that we've made, I think, significant improvements is on the sales side, where we've really focused the sales organization on those direct-to-customer relationships and club is a big part of that.

And I think as we've improved the relationships with our club buyers, we've done a much better job of articulating our value proposition, how we perform in the category, and that has enabled us to, I think, get back some of our momentum that we mitigated a bit over the last year, 18 months. And so that's an example of just the team being really focused and sharing great consumer insights that I mentioned. We're using those in a much better way. We've got shopper insights that are customer-specific, and we're using that -- and so again, it's focusing the organization and then enabling them to go win.

And so this is an example of them winning back something in club where we have a great value proposition. We have a great product and great taste. And so it was getting that back, and we did it. And so we're excited about that and excited to continue to focus on where the biggest opportunities are. So yes, again, an example of the team just working really well and leveraging our insights and shopper work.

Operator: And the next question is going to come from Robert Moskow with TD Cowen.

Robert Moskow: I had a question about the ongoing discussions you're having about your promotion plan with FDM customers and merchandising plan. I just want to make sure I understand what the key discussions are about. You raised your list prices and you have one big customer that I believe you had some very aggressive merchandising activity with in fiscal '26. So is the discussion about how high the promoted price point should go and whether there might be any like price clips you don't want to go over? Because I imagine from a consumer standpoint, there are certain price points that really move the product.

As part of this price increase, is your promoted price point going to have to go up as well?

Michael Axelrod: Rob, we have a very strong relationship with this customer, supported by very healthy and strong consumption trends, which are really driving the category growth for them. It's delayed given the price increase. I mean given the magnitude of the increase, certain promotional plans for Q2 have been slightly delayed. We believe and I believe we're positioned well to secure the merchandising program. But just given the discussions that are -- they continue to be ongoing, we thought it'd be appropriate to include a range of scenarios for our guidance. So the guidance includes the timing of the promotion and the impact of the promotion in our guidance. So I feel like we're making great progress.

It's just been a slight delay because of the price increase.

Operator: And the next question is going to come from Matt Smith with Stifel.

Matthew Smith: Paul, it's been a pleasure to work with you. I wanted to follow up on the $100 million supply chain savings program. You've talked about supply constraints easing for the category. Can you give a little more detail as to the scope of the program beyond the $25 million in fiscal '27? And then relatedly or perhaps relatedly, what is the margin impact or the impact to inflation from lower volumes through your existing supply chain contracts this year? Is that a discrete headwind that abates? Or is that -- were you able to renegotiate those contracts coming into this year?

Michael Axelrod: Yes. So thanks for your question. I think at least $100 million of cost savings are coming out of COGS, and that's coming out of manufacturing, packaging, procurement and logistics. These are all gross margin initiatives. And as part of our full review that we're doing, we will include SG&A. But the biggest potential here is on COGS where we can really leverage the scale of our brand. And so I think that, that -- the 3 years, I think it's about a 6% cost takeout -- at least a 6% cost takeout in these COGS. And we have flexibility to use those savings in our brands, absorb inflation and also drive profitability.

So I think as we come out of the strategic review, we'll be more clear about how we see those dollars and where they're going to go.

Paul Rode: And then, Matt, on the second part of your question, our guidance does reflect our current thinking on the potential -- any potential minimum volume commitments based on -- it's obviously a range from the high to the low. So there -- we do contemplate any minimum volume commitments and that we would need to pay. And we're continuing to work those, as you said, to either minimize them or to potentially eliminate them, but those -- we have contemplated that in our guidance.

Operator: And the next question will come from Stephen Powers with Deutsche Bank.

Stephen Robert Powers: Paul, my appreciation and well wishes as well. It's been a pleasure working with you. Mike, I wanted to ask on that same $100 million of savings just from a different perspective, and you alluded to it in your answer just a second ago. But it's a big chunk of savings, especially as you think about incremental savings as we look at SG&A. But you've also outlined a meaningful agenda of capability enhancements across consumer insights, marketing, innovation, retail planning, commercial execution, et cetera. So I guess just as you sit here looking at the longer term, just should we think about that savings pool is more just a gross funding pool to offset that reinvestment and some inflation?

Or just your confidence that a meaningful portion of it can ultimately flow through to structurally higher margins?

Michael Axelrod: Yes. So I think we do continue to do the work to ensure where we think the best ROI is going to be on the business. And there are a lot of -- there's a tremendous amount of initiatives going on across the business. And so we're organizing in order to execute with excellence, and I'll talk about that as we go through Q2 here in the future. But I think a lot of that savings is we're going to unlock a lot of value also through being more effective on our promotions and the work we're doing to -- we're doing work to relaunch packaging and formulations that will come out later this year, fiscal year as well.

And so I think as we think through all of those different areas, a portion of that, at least $100 million over the next 3 years, a portion of that will go into profit and a portion of that will continue to fund the business. I think at the end of the day, the core shake has -- we want to make sure we have the best value proposition in the market with our core shake, and that's the work we're undertaking. And so I anticipate more color on that coming into Q2.

Operator: And our next question is going to come from Yasmine Deswandhy with Bank of America.

Yasmine Deswandhy: Paul, great working with you over the years. I know there's been a lot of discussion around club on this call, and I just had another clarifying question. Premier Protein RTD consumption in club actually saw meaningful improvement in Q4 quarter-over-quarter. It flipped positive. I'm just trying to square that into thinking about next year with -- you're getting into pretty easy compares through the first 3 quarters of next year on club consumption for RTD shakes. So is it that it will still be negative in the first quarter? Or will it kind of be positive throughout the year as you're kind of lapping some of these easy compares?

Paul Rode: Yes. I mean our guidance includes obviously a range of outcomes, including by channel. We don't -- we haven't gone down disclosing our guidance on channel. I'd say at a high level, we continue to expect strong growth in FDM and e-commerce, and we continue to expect that the competitive environment in club will stay elevated. As we talked about on this call, we're pursuing a number of opportunities to improve our trends, getting back the incremental pallet, obviously, that we expected to lose was part of that and some of these regional tests that we're doing also are parts of that.

So again, there's a number of opportunities we're pursuing that we think can benefit the near term and long term. But ultimately, we feel good about where we are with club, but it's continuing to work to improve the trends there and to get it to growth.

Operator: And the next question will come from Robert Dickerson with BTIG.

Robert Dickerson: And thank you, Paul. I guess just a question on the DSD capability. I think you had a comment in the prepared remarks how you look to leverage that, that would add some to the top line. I heard you make a comment too on potentially signing recently new C-store distribution contracts. So just like as we think about the broader strategic review that's ongoing, where does DSD actually start to play an incremental kind of distribution opportunity piece of the business, and clearly, I assume that's all outsourced, right? You're not thinking actually building in-house capabilities. So I'm just trying to understand where DSD fits, how that changes over time?

And does that just give you a bigger opportunity for kind of increased channel diversity?

Michael Axelrod: Yes. So I'll take this. Convenience represents, I think, an attractive opportunity for us as consumers expand -- as we expand our consumption occasions and reach new households. It's a great way to get trial of our products -- the right products. And just in terms of the size of the channel, it's about 10% of $10 billion. So it's about $1 billion channel. And our priority is really to establish the right distribution economics, execution capabilities and consumer proposition as we scale. We do need to invest and have invested in building that capability internally because it does require resources that have the relevant experience in building that out.

We have started with regional distribution partners and national convenience chains. And I think for '27, we expect a modest contribution of about 1% of sales growth with an opportunity to grow that over time. It's a very exciting channel for growth, but we also have to grow and focus on leading in club, mass and our e-commerce partners where there's also a tremendous amount of growth opportunity.

Operator: And our next question is going to come from Glenn West with William Blair.

Glenn West: This is Glenn on for Jon Anderson. Just a quick one at the end here. Over the course of the past year, you guys bought back quite a bit of stock, and I appreciate you're at 3.6x leverage, targeting below 3 by the end of the year. I guess I'm just curious -- and Paul, you mentioned capital allocation includes returning cash to shareholders. Do purchases, are they going to continue or resume before you reach that 3x level or only after? Or just how do you guys rank buybacks with the debt pay down?

Michael Axelrod: Yes. Glenn, our immediate focus right now, our priority is strengthening the business and reducing leverage. We believe there are compelling opportunities to create value through just organic growth and improved profitability in the business. And as our balance sheet strengthens, share repurchases can be an attractive use of that capital. I think we'll continue to evaluate opportunities that create shareholder value. And that's what we'll focus on here.

Operator: Thank you. And this does conclude the Q&A session, and this will also conclude today's conference call. We want to thank you for participating, and you may now disconnect.

#3123. IntelliProve raises €2.7M to take its face scan health check to robots

The Belgian startup’s software reads heart rate, breathing, and blood pressure through a standard camera. IntelliProve told TNW a third of the money goes to certification as it eyes humanoid robots.

IntelliProve’s founders, from left: Brecht Dhuyvetters, Joeri Tulkens, Maxime Mattelin and Tanguy Sanglet.

Belgian healthtech startup IntelliProve has raised €2.7 million in seed funding to take its camera-based health scan from virtual care apps to humanoid robots. Miles Ahead led the round. Home nursing organisation Wit-Gele Kruis, the imec.istart Fund, and several business angels also took part.

The Ghent company’s software reads heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV), breathing, and blood pressure from a 30-second face scan. It needs only a standard camera, and no cuff. Care providers, insurers, and wellbeing platforms in more than 50 countries already build it into their apps, IntelliProve said.

“This funding round allows us to invest in technology and growth. We can open conversations with robotics companies and virtual care partners worldwide, while doubling down on the data and certification that make all of it possible,” co-CEO Joeri Tulkens told TNW. “Our ambition is simple: a health sensing layer that care can rely on, on any camera.”

Roughly a third of the money goes to regulatory work and a third to further research, Tulkens told TNW. The last third goes to commercial growth, including robotics deployments.

IntelliProve already holds a CE mark as a Class I medical device under the EU Medical Device Regulation. That mark covers its core signal acquisition engine, the technology that pulls physiological signals from facial video, Tulkens said. The company is now working towards Class IIa certification, but would not say yet which measurements that will cover.

The scan on IntelliProve’s website is a lighter version for developers to test. It returns heart rate, HRV, and respiratory rate. Blood pressure is available to integration partners, Tulkens said.

The technique is called remote photoplethysmography, or rPPG. Each heartbeat changes the colour of facial skin very slightly, and a camera can pick up the change. IntelliProve’s software tracks the skin as the person moves, extracts the pulse signal, and estimates blood pressure from the shape of the pulse wave with an in-house deep learning model.

The company says its models are validated on more than 6 million data points. In its own tests, 97.6% of heart rate readings fell within five beats per minute of a reference device, its press kit says.

IntelliProve works with TU Delft, Ghent University Hospital, and Wit-Gele Kruis, which is also an investor.

The company wants the same layer in humanoid robots heading into homes and care facilities. Investors are backing robot makers, from Agile Robots’ $500M round to Minerva Humanoids’ pre-seed. A robot would offer the scan with the cameras it already has. It would then pass the values to a person, who decides what happens next.

IntelliProve said it already works with selected robotics partners. It did not name them when TNW asked. The funding will also pay for more data across skin tones, ages, lighting, and devices. It also covers certification beyond Europe.

“Whether the scan runs on a smartphone or on a humanoid robot, the bar stays the same,” co-founder and CTO Tanguy Sanglet said in a statement.

I love a hack, especially when it comes to training legs. If you don't want to lift heavy weights but you do want to improve lower-body strength and mobility, let me introduce you to one exercise that will change the game for you.

Check out the exercise below, how to do it, and the benefits for your body.

The Cossack Squat is an underrated bodyweight exercise. Unlike standard squats or lunges, you load one leg at a time with a deep lateral (side-to-side) plane of motion, which builds single-leg strength, adductor flexibility and resilience and joint mobility.

Here's a step-by-step guide on how to do them:

This move hits a lot of muscles, including your core for trunk stabilization, and your hip flexors, quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves and lower back.

The much deeper sitting position and lateral direction hit the outer glutes and inner thighs much harder than regular squats or lunges, which unlocks mobility. Plus, a deep stretch in your groin and adductor muscles and better mobility in your hips, knees and ankles will make other exercises, like overhead squats, feel more achievable.

What I love most is that unilateral loading creates plenty of tension in the working muscles to achieve overload without weights. At the same time, you build frontal-plane strength by moving side-to-side, which is important for targeting muscles like the adductors and outer hips. Strengthening as many muscles as you can means your body will be more resilient during rotation or big, heavy lifts.

Finally, you can also tick the box for loaded mobility, which means actively increasing range of motion in your joints while loading the joints and muscles naturally.

Hold on to something for support if you find depth or balance difficult. You can also elevate your heel on a wedge or similar. Limited ankle mobility and short Achilles tendons will make it tricky to keep the heel pressed down, so don't be too disheartened if you struggle here.

You can add weight to this move to place your hands behind your head or raise them into the air to make Cossack squats more challenging and test thoracic mobility and balance.

Pause for three seconds at the bottom without letting your hamstring rest on your calf, or transition smoothly from side to side.

#3120. ChatGPT app gains enhanced Live Dictation streaming without 10-minute limit

ChatGPT dictation is getting a boost today. OpenAI has updated the speech-to-text feature with Live Dictation that improves both speed and reliability. The enhanced dictation update also removes the 10-minute limit.

“Dictation in ChatGPT is getting faster and more reliable,” OpenAI announced on X.

“With Live Dictation, your speech turns into text as you talk, so you spend less time waiting for your message to finish transcribing,” the company continued.

Atty Eleti, who works on voice features at OpenAI, added that the 10-minute dictation limit has also been removed as part of the dictation streaming upgrade.

More details from today’s app update release notes below:

Dictation in ChatGPT is getting faster and more reliable.

With Live Dictation, your speech turns into text as you talk, so you spend less time waiting for your message to finish transcribing. Tap or click on the waveform to show or hide text as you go. We’ve also removed the 10-minute recording limit.

Live Dictation is rolling out globally to all ChatGPT plans on iOS, Android, web, and the desktop app.

The first Apple e-Series model may be older, but it still has a lot going for it too. In fact, the only key differences between it and the iPhone 17e are the lack of MagSafe and the fact it has an A18 chip.

Samsung's take on the passport-shaped foldable is easily one of the best phones of the year. The shorter, wider design is comfortable to use, and the anti-glare screen makes it perfect for watching movies or working no matter the conditions. The battery could be better, and the lack of telephoto lens isn't ideal, but this is a fantastic deal on a foldable you can buy right now.

If you'd prefer a bigger screen and telephoto zoom camera, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is the option for you. It's a little bit more expensive, but you get more screen space, camera resolution and battery capacity for your money.

The Z Flip 8 is less exciting by comparison, but it still gets you the foldable experience in a compact form. You have the normal-size 6.9-inch phone display, a pair of solid cameras and a cover display that can run full Android apps without requiring you to flip the thing open.

If you want a book-style foldable with a heavy discount, there's always the Galaxy Z Fold 7. It's the same shape and size as the Z fold 8 Ultra, though it lacks the Flex Titanium crease-free display, higher performance and larger batteries of the newer model. But it's also a few hundred dollars cheaper.

If the latest Galaxy S26 is up your alley, Walmart has knocked it back down to $799, reversing the recent price hike. You get the latest Galaxy AI features, a 6.3-inch OLED display, a 4,300 mAh battery, 50MP main camera, 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage standard.

If you want a bigger screen and less-flashy hardware, the S25 Plus has your back — and a price to match. It has a 6.7-inch display, 45W charging, 50MP rear cameras, a 4,900 mAh battery, and all the latest Galaxy AI features.

The super thin Galaxy S25 Edge is still available, and it's been given a nice Black Friday discount. So if you want a skinny phone with two solid cameras running Android, now's your chance.

If Samsung's price hikes have you down, the Galaxy S26 FE is the perfect solution — offering flagship level specs at a newly-discounted price. For your money you get solid camera and battery performance, including a telephoto lens, and a large 6.7-inch display and the latest Galaxy AI software.

The Fan Edition lineup is a great way to get flagship features at a discount, and the S25 FE was no exception. It may not be as new or powerful as the S26 FE, but the physical differences between the two are fairly minimal. That said, I do prefer this model's more premium-looking back glass.

The Pixel 11 is more than half off over at Mint Mobile, and the only catch is you need to sign up for Mint's Unlimited data plan — at a cost of $180 for a year. Though that still makes this an excellent discount, especially if you like AI features and speedy access to Android updates.

If you want more out of your Pixel, Mint has knocked $505 off the cost of the Pixel 11 Pro. For your money you get the HiLight notification alert, better cameras, a brighter display and strong battery life. But again you do need that $180 unlimited plan.

If you want a larger screen, the Pixel 11 Pro XL is the exact same phone, only bigger and with a larger battery. It's discounted from $1,299 to $794 at Mint.

It may not be the most exciting foldable around, nor is this the biggest discount, but if you want a Pixel Fold device this is the best discount around right now. Just be aware that you need to pay an extra $180 for Mint's Unlimited plan to be eligible.

One of the best cheap phones you can buy, the Nothing 4a Pro offers great cameras and battery life, including a 50MP telephoto lens — which is a rarity at this price point. Also included is the custom Glyph Matrix LED display on the back, Nothing's latest AI features and solid performance.

If you want the latest and most compact foldable, the Razr 2026 is on sale at Mint Mobile. However, the discount requires you to sign up for a 12-month Unlimited plan for $180. Still, you get a large foldable display, strong performance, a crazy 4,800 mAh battery and a range of Motorola's AI features.

If you want a cheap compact foldable without the added data plan, the 2025 Motorola Razr is the one to pick. You get a large bright foldable display, an assortment of AI features and a cover display that can run all your Android apps — even ones that may not be optimized for it.

If the standard Razr isn't cutting it for you, the Plus model has a little more to offer. It's got a faster 165Hz refresh rate, a 4,000 mAh battery, 12GB of RAM, 256GB of storage, and a pair of 50MP (main and telephoto) cameras. Plus a 32MP selfie camera.

The Razr Ultra is almost half price right now, with the same 165Hz refresh rate, 512GB of storage, a boosted 16GB of RAM, a 50MP selfie camera and a crazy 4,500 nits of screen brightness.
